newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CPI seen up after crown crisis - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Czech CPI seen up after crown crisis - analysts.

text.p: The downtrend of Czech inflation (CPI) should come to a halt in June due to seasonal factors and possible inflationary effects of crown's recent weakening, a survey of six economists showed on Monday.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) is scheduled to release June CPI data on Tuesday at 0700 GMT, and economists forecast an average increase of about 0.9 percent month-on-month, up from 0.1 percent in May. The range was 0.6-1.1 percent.
Since December the year-on-year rate has steadily dropped from 8.6 percent to a record low of 6.3 percent in May.
The survey showed that a 0.9 percent month-on-month figure would put the year-on-year rate for June at about 6.4 percent.
"I expect inflation to rise a little bit compared to the previous month due to seasonal changes and because of the weakening of the crown," said Jiri Krovak, chief economist at WoodCommerz in Prague.
"But it is difficult because there is no empirical evidence that inflation will be affected by the exchange rate...It's just a feeling this time...."
The crown came under a heavy downward pressure at the end of May as speculators targeted the currency as overvalued.
The CNB was eventually forced on May 27 to float the currency which fell by approximately 10 percent.

"It's tough to say what the effect of the currency fluctuation will be, but if food prices -- a major component of the inflation basket -- hold steady, it may not be a major jump," said Boris Gomez, an analyst at ING Barings in Prague.
In June 1996, foodstuffs were the main factor behind a 0.8 percent month-on-month rise in inflation, which put the year-on-year rate at 8.4 percent.
WoodCommerz's Krovak also pointed to historical evidence that shows Czech inflation usually rises during periods of a weaker deutschemark.
"The most decisive influence on inflation so far has been the cross rate between the dollar and the deutschemark -- the stronger the dollar the higher the inflation in this country," he said.
